podcast.title: Diverse Post-Ben Folds Five Career
podcast.body: Since his time with Ben Folds Five, Ben Folds has pursued a highly varied career, releasing solo albums, collaborating with diverse artists like William Shatner and "Weird Al" Yankovic, composing Hollywood film soundtracks, acting, judging an NBC talent show, serving as an artistic director for a symphony orchestra, hosting a podcast, and writing a memoir. This extensive range of activities demonstrates his versatile talents. "Since then, Ben Foltz has released a number of albums on his own, collaborated with everyone from William Shatton or to Weird Al, written soundtracks for Hollywood films, Dunsome Acting, appeared as a judge on an NBC talent show, served as an artistic director to a symphony orchestra, hosted a podcast and written a memoir."

podcast.title: Formation of Ben Folds Five and "Punk Rock for Sissies"
podcast.body: After numerous dead ends with other bands and gigs, Ben Folds found success upon moving back home to North Carolina and forming Ben Folds Five. He characterized their unique sound as "Punk Rock for Sissies," defining a style that blended punk energy with piano-driven melodies. "It wasn't until he moved back home to North Carolina and formed a band he called Ben Foltz Five that things started to click. He called his music, Punk Rock for Sissies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Percussion Scholarship and Return to Piano
podcast.body: Ben Folds initially received a scholarship to a music school in Miami for percussion, a promising start that ultimately ended with him losing the scholarship. Following this, he intensely returned to the piano, dedicating six months to running scales with a metronome "like a freak." "But then he got a scholarship to a music school in Miami for percussion, which started off promising, but then he crashed out and lost a scholarship. You head back to the piano and spent, he says, six months running scales with a metronome like a freak."

podcast.title: Primary Influence for Joe Jackson
podcast.body: Alt Rock Piano Man Ben Folds has publicly stated that Joe Jackson was a primary influence on his hits with his band, Ben Folds Five. This acknowledgment highlights Joe Jackson's significant impact on subsequent generations of musicians, particularly pianists in the alternative rock genre. "Alt Rock Piano Man Ben Folds has claimed Joe Jackson was a primary influence on his hits with the Ben Folds V."

podcast.title: Unexpected Piano Acquisition and Early Influences
podcast.body: Ben Folds' musical journey began at age nine when his carpenter father accepted a piano as payment from a customer unable to pay for a job. This serendipitous event allowed Ben to become a fan of Elton John and Billy Joel, prompting him to learn their songs by ear from the radio. "The best thing that ever happened to Ben was when his father brought home a piano. He was a carpenter where the customer couldn't pay for a job, so he was paid with a piano. This was perfect for nine-year-old Ben because he'd become a fan of Elton John and Billy Joel and began learning songs off the radio."
